name: Crossed-Subcube Pendant Contraction Obstructions
definition: Let $X=\{a,b,p,q\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\mathbin{\dot\cup}V$. Delete from $2^X$ every $\{a\}\cup S$ and $\{a,b\}\cup S$ for $S\subseteq U$, and every $\{b\}\cup T$ and $\{a,b\}\cup T$ for $T\subseteq V$. If $\alpha=1$, also delete $\{a,p\}\cup S$ for $S\subseteq U$; if $\beta=1$, also delete $\{b,q\}\cup T$ for $T\subseteq V$. From the remaining learning space, attach a new pendant coordinate above every state while retaining the lone lower state $R=\{b,p\}\cup V$.
parameters: $d=|X|\ge4$; disjoint coordinate blocks $U,V$; and $\alpha,\beta\in\{0,1\}$. The resulting family has $d+1$ active coordinates and $2^d-(2+\alpha)2^{|U|}-(2+\beta)2^{|V|}+2$ states.
canonical_form: The source records the ordered crossed blocks, the two distinguished free coordinates, and the two optional half-wing flags. At $U=V=\varnothing$, only $\alpha+\beta$ distinguishes the three pointed base types up to the stated identifications.
recognition: A construction certificate lists the two deleted wings, verifies the complementary endpoints, and checks that their exact contraction-repair sets cover all base coordinates.
comments: Every member is contraction-minimal outside learning-space graphs. This is not a pc-minimal forbidden family because learning-space graphs are not closed under convex restrictions.
